key_insight: Harness-Zero shows that an agent can learn from a strong, task-specific harness during training and then operate more effectively without needing that exact harness at deployment. In simple terms, it turns a “best harness available” into a transferable skill.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the mismatch between training and deployment in agent systems: the best external harness often depends on the domain, task instance, and model, making it hard to use one universal harness without sacrificing performance.
method: Use a domain- or instance-optimized harness as a training-time guide for the agent.
Distill the behavior and benefits of the optimized harness into the agent itself, reducing reliance on external orchestration at test time.
Enable agents to generalize better across tasks by learning harness-like decision patterns rather than depending on a fixed deployment harness.
impact: This matters because practitioners can get stronger agent performance without maintaining a large, brittle collection of specialized harnesses at inference time. It simplifies deployment while preserving much of the benefit of task-specific orchestration.
